rules.title: Boston tenant eviction protections home rule petition (H.3744, 193rd session)
rules.requirement: This proposal never became law. It would have let Boston adopt its own tenant eviction protections, but it was sent to a study order and died when the 2023–2024 session ended.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would have authorized the City of Boston to adopt tenant eviction protections. The bill text is not in the source, so the details are unknown.
rules.reason: This is a single failed home rule petition. It stays separate from the enacted law because failed proposals are never merged into enacted law.

rules.title: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act: tenant rights notice required with a notice to quit or lease non-renewal
rules.requirement: If your Boston landlord, or an owner after foreclosure, gives you a Notice to Quit or a notice that your lease won't be renewed, they must give you a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time. They must also send a copy to the City's Office of Housing Stability. If you don't get the notice, report it to the Office of Fair Housing and Equity (617-635-2500 or 311).
rules.key_value: Rights notice must come with the Notice to Quit or non-renewal notice; $300/day fines for second and later offenses
rules.coverage_conditions: Covers all landlords and foreclosing owners ending a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston, whether by eviction, lease non-renewal, or asking occupants to leave after foreclosure. Tenants cannot waive these rights.
rules.exemptions: Residences in hospitals, skilled nursing or health facilities, and non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities.
rules.citation: Boston City Ordinances § 10-11.7 (Housing Stability Notification Act)
rules.penalty: Enforced by the Inspectional Services Department: a warning for a first offense, then $300 per day for second and later offenses. A violation does not stop the eviction.
rules.reason: This is a single candidate describing Boston's enacted Housing Stability Notification Act. It is a different law from the failed home rule petition.
